title: Kernel Sentinel: cascade autotuner for architecture and sequence-length aware kernel routing
creator: Rishi Kapoor
description: Problem: our serving runtime currently uses static kernel selection heuristics that degrade across heterogeneous customer workloads (mixed sequence lengths, multi-GPU topologies, and varied quantization profiles). We see p95 latency spikes on mixed-prefill/decode workloads and suboptimal cost/perf on T4 vs A800 families. Goal: implement a lightweight, online ‘Kernel Sentinel’ that orchestrates a cascade of microprobes and a compact selector model to pick kernels per-request (or per-route) based on architecture, token-phase, and recent latency/cost telemetry. The design must be low-overhead (<0.5% additional latency on median) and provide robust safety fallbacks to maintain SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Sentinel performs an online microprobe (<=3 candidate kernels) within first N warm requests and chooses a kernel that reduces p95 latency by >=10% for mixed-length workloads relative to baseline. 2) No increase in error rate or memory OOM incidents during rollout. 3) Canary for at least two customers for one week with telemetry showing stable tails. 4) Automated rollback triggers for >20% tail degradation or >15% cost increase.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Rishi Kapoor: Triage complete. Assigned to Maya. Initial spike analysis attached (link to internal dashboard). Identified two root causes: (a) static kernel tables tuned for median-seqlen; (b) no topology-aware bandwidth penalty in the cost model.

2026-02-24 - Maya Chen: Drafted proposal for a three-stage autotune pipeline: 1) lightweight token-phase classifier (prefill vs decode phase detection + median-prefix-length sketch); 2) microprobe runner executing short microbenchmarks (microsecond-scale) across 2-4 kernel candidates; 3) selector (rule-based fallback + small logistic regression) that blends microprobe results with historical telemetry. Posted PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/kernel-sentinel (internal).

2026-02-28 - Tomás Rivera (review): Asked for clearer safety constraints and rollback windows; suggested adding a per-GPU resource budget and limiting probe frequency by customer tier. Also requested compatibility with dedicated/GPU-pooled topologies.

2026-03-03 - Maya Chen: Ran local microbench experiments on A800 and T4; microprobe overhead measured ~0.15% p50 and ~0.4% p95 for low QPS routes. Preliminary results: sentinel reduced p95 by 12% on mixed-prefill workload (internal sim). Uploaded microbench artifacts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8421

2026-03-06 - QA: Found a regression in multi-GPU NCCL bandwidth estimation that caused the selector to pick a high-memory kernel on 8xA100 runs. Added dependency to fix bandwidth estimator (ENG-432092).

2026-03-08 - Maya Chen: Added safety-net: probe-explore budget per GPU, exponential backoff on probes per-route, and immediate fallback to conservative kernel when tail exceeds threshold. Updated rollout plan to include a 24h passive observation window before active switching.

2026-03-10 - Rishi Kapoor: Design review complete. Approved canary for two internal customers and one external beta partner (privacy-safe telemetry). Next: implement microprobe harness and selector, integrate with runtime routing layer, add telemetry dashboards and rollback alerts.
implementation_notes: Key components: 1) Phase detector: sketch-based estimator (count-min + histogram of prefix lengths) to classify request phase within 1ms. 2) Microprobe harness: per-GPU sentinel worker that runs short decode/prefill kernels on tiny super-batches (batch size 1-4) measuring p50/p95 and memory delta. Probes record latency, memory, and NVLink/NCCL penalty estimate. 3) Selector: logistic regression + heuristic blend that prefers lower-tail latency but penalizes memory headroom <10%. 4) Safety & rollout: passive mode, then active switching with canary customers, automated rollback triggers (tail↑>20% or cost↑>15%), and manual override in Console.
testing_plan: Unit tests for probe harness and phase detector, integration tests that simulate mixed prefills and long-decodes, end-to-end canary against synthetic workload (range of seqLen 8-4096). Performance bench harness will run on A800, T4, and 8xA100 multi-GPU config. SLOs measured: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, memory headroom, and cost-per-million-tokens.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal passive runs (2 days) on low-impact routes. 2) Internal canary (3 customers) active switching (1 week). 3) External beta partner (1 week). 4) Gradual global ramp with circuit-breaker thresholds. All steps produce dashboarded telemetry and automatic rollback hooks.
